text:
Reza: Heads-up — after the 03:10 BMC push to us-central2-rack7 a subset of nodes are toggling the secure-boot bit and failing to present GPUs to the host. ~12 nodes so far, mostly in rack7A. :frowning_face:
Olivia: on it. can you paste dmesg/ipmitool output from one affected box?
Reza: grabbing now, here's the ipmictl snippet: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.4.7.23 -U admin -P **** sel list` -> shows repeated 'EFI variable write failed' and `SecureBoot: Enabled` flips during boot. Also netconsole shows `kvm: no devices` on the initramfs line.
Sam: that's consistent with the BMC firmware toggling the UEFI attr during postflash. rack7A was in canary group. Did the deploy-bot report any rollback?
oncall-bot: deploy-bot reported success for 03:10 canary on 7A (ids: r7a-01..r7a-24), no automatic rollback triggered.
Reza: no auto rollback. We saw ~50% of the canary reboot cycle end with `GPU not found` from nvme/PCI probe. Hostd fails provisioning jobs and stays in `maintenance` until manual force-reprobe.
Aisha: how many GPU instances impacted? rough numbers matter for paging and cost.
Reza: approx 34 GPUs offline, estimated 6% capacity hit for us-central2. If this persists we start evicting long jobs and cost goes up from cross-region fallbacks.
Olivia: immediate plan: 1) pause the rollout to remaining racks, 2) trigger manual BMC rollback on canary nodes, 3) run reprovision script with `bmc-tool repair-uefi --trustdb=legacy` on affected. Agree?
Sam: +1. Add: collect `journalctl -b -u oob-agent` and `curl http://10.4.7.23:8080/api/v1/bmc/vars` for a reproducible trace. Save to /tmp/bug-traces/r7a-<node>.log.
Reza: running collection now. pasted one log chunk: ```Oct 14 03:12:04 r7a-03 oob-agent[1123]: firmware_flash: completed, result=ok
Oct 14 03:12:07 r7a-03 kernel: efivar: failed to write variable SecureBoot, -5
Oct 14 03:12:07 r7a-03 kernel: pci 0000:03:00.0: BAR0: assigned to non-prefetchable memory
Oct 14 03:12:09 r7a-03 hostd[5321]: GPUs: probe failed -> index -19```
Aisha: notes for postmortem: which firmware version pattern? is this only the 1.2.9->1.2.10 delta?
Reza: yes, looks like 1.2.10 introduced a change in the UEFI variable write path when `bmc-secure-verify=on`. Old 1.2.9 didn't hit the path.
Olivia: I've paused remaining canaries and turned off the scheduled rollout for the rest of us-central2. Sam, can infra-runbook-bot create a rollback run with the exact node list? Also include an automated health-check that verifies GPUs are enumerated post-reboot.
oncall-bot: rollback run created: RB-174210-1 targeting r7a-01..r7a-12, r7a-15..r7a-18. Health-check: `nvidia-smi -L` + `lspci | grep -i nvidia` required.
Sam: executing manual rollback on r7a-03 and r7a-05 now. status: r7a-03 rollback started, r7a-05 rollback completed, GPUs re-enumerated, jobs resumed. :thumbsup:
Reza: good signal. Still need to triage why some nodes flip SecureBoot after successful write. Could be NV storage wear or timing race during early PCI init.
Aisha: capture a sysfs snapshot and BIOS variables from one failing node and one recovered node: `/sys/firmware/efi/vars` and `dmidecode -t bios`. Put diffs in the bug tracker.
Olivia: tagging firmware team and setting a follow-up: revert 1.2.10 from canary and block re-release until we have repro and fix. Also open a billing ticket — if we need cross-region fallbacks >24h finance needs alert.
Reza: FYI I saw one node with `BMC: kexec-triggered recovery` log — might be related to watchdog. We should verify watchdog-writes aren't racing with efivars.
Sam: created a short mitigation: add a preflash lock that disables secure-verify while writing vars and re-enables after kmm sync; requires BMC change but could be toggled via management ACL quickly. Testing in isolated lab.
Olivia: ok. For oncall: if more than 10 nodes flip in a region escalate to SEV-2 and begin cross-region job draining to avoid SLA hits. For now we remain SEV-3.
Reza: I'll annotate the incident and include the saved logs + node list in the incident ticket.
Aisha: thanks. keep updates short here. :eyes:
